entries.content:
The Chozo are a race of highly intelligent, bird-like extraterrestrials (their Japanese name means bird-human race): beaked, feathered humanoids with taloned hands and unusually long lives. Their origins are unknown even to themselves; their own records on Tallon IV admit they were unsure where they came from. At its height their civilization stretched across many worlds, among them Zebes, SR388, Tallon IV, Elysia and ZDR, and they exchanged knowledge with the Luminoth, the Ylla, the Bryyonians and humanity. Luminoth records remember them among "a vast number of enlightened minds"; Bryyonian records call the Chozo, Luminoth and Ylla "stellar brethren".

They were builders and teachers. On Elysia they raised the floating research station SkyTown and created the Elysian mechanoids to maintain it. On Zebes they built the supercomputer Mother Brain to govern the planet. On SR388 their Thoha scientists engineered the Metroids to prey on the X Parasites. Their powered battle armor became Samus Aran's Power Suit. Per the manga, they also helped found the Galactic Federation. They urged allied peoples to balance new technology against their native cultures; Bryyo ignored the warning and tore itself apart in civil war.

Their deepest mark on the galaxy is one person. After Space Pirates under Ridley razed the colony K-2L, the Chozo of Zebes took in the orphaned child Samus Aran, integrated Chozo DNA with hers so that her frail human body could survive Zebes and bear their armor, raised and trained her, and gave her the Power Suit before she left to serve the Galactic Federation. Two Chozo are known to have contributed their DNA to her: Gray Voice (per the manga) and Raven Beak of the Mawkin tribe, who was present at her adoption (Metroid Dread). The Chozo of Tallon IV, in their inscribed Chozo Lore, remember "the child we found so long ago" and name her the Hatchling, the Newborn and the Entrusted One, the one who would bear their legacy.

The Chozo are now all but gone. Zebes was destroyed. The Tallon IV Chozo passed beyond the physical world or became the corrupted Turned, the Chozo Ghosts. The Thoha were massacred by Raven Beak; the Mawkin of ZDR were consumed by the X; Quiet Robe and Raven Beak, the last two Chozo known to be alive, both died during the ZDR incident, and ZDR itself was destroyed. Whether any Chozo survive elsewhere is unknown; none have shown themselves. Samus, carrying their blood, wearing their armor and raised in their teachings, is in practice the last heir of the Chozo. See also Old Bird, Gray Voice, Thoha, Mawkin, Chozo Statues, Chozo Memories, Chozo Lore, Chozo Ghosts.
entries.notes: Main overview; only entry carrying the bare key 'Chozo'. Physical description limited to what official depictions show. 'Helped found the Federation' softened from Metroid Wiki's 'founded', labelled per the manga.

entries.comment: Chozo: Chozo history, philosophy and decline
entries.content:
Chozo history is a long arc from expansion to withdrawal. Roughly 1,500 years before Samus's time the Chozo began building SkyTown among the clouds of Elysia, hovering research pods from which they studied the cosmos. About fifty years in they created the Elysian mechanoids to handle construction and maintenance, and a Chozo researcher there detected a distant living planet, later known as Phaaze, before the data was lost. In the Elysian year 400 the Chozo left SkyTown, bound for Tallon IV, to share their knowledge with other races, asking the Elysians to keep searching for the sentient world.

On Zebes the Chozo built a civilization and the supercomputer Mother Brain, and there they later raised Samus Aran. On SR388 the Thoha and Mawkin tribes created and then struggled to contain the Metroids. On Tallon IV they made a deliberate break with their past: they chose to eschew a civilization of advanced technology, building halls of stone and woven branches around ancient trees and living guided by the providence of the universe. Their sages taught that "the truths of the universe hide within the tumbling currents of time's flow"; in time many Chozo developed visions of past and future, which they took as a sign of their burgeoning harmonization with the infinite. Those visions showed them a Worm that would devour the world from within, and a Defender who might stop it.

The Chozo preached restraint and understanding. Old Bird taught the young Samus that befriending and understanding others can solve problems (per the manga), and the Chozo warned the people of Bryyo against adopting technology too fast. Not every Chozo held to this: the Mawkin were a warrior tribe, and their leader Raven Beak lived by the creed "Hadar sen olmen", power is everything.

Their decline had several causes. Per the manga, the science that gave the Chozo unusual longevity compromised their ability to reproduce, and their numbers and strength dwindled; Old Bird told Samus plainly that the Chozo were a declining species. On Zebes, Mother Brain turned on its makers and the Space Pirates expelled the Chozo (per the manga). On Tallon IV a meteor, a Leviathan, brought the Great Poison, Phazon, about fifty years before Samus arrived; the Chozo could not cure it, sealed its source beneath the Cradle behind a lock of twelve Artifacts, and then faded: their minds weakened as they drifted through time and space, many passed on, and those who remained became the Turned. Their last record speaks of leaving the planet pristine and withdrawing beyond the illusion of the physical world. On SR388 Raven Beak's massacre of the Thoha, and on ZDR the X Parasites, ended the last known living Chozo.

Today the Chozo survive only in their ruins, statues and records, in their creations (the Elysians, the Metroids' legacy, Samus's Power Suit), and in Samus herself, who carries Chozo DNA and was raised in their ways. See also Thoha, Mawkin, Chozo Lore, Chozo Ghosts, Elysians, Mother Brain.
entries.notes: Elysian dates from the SkyTown page; Tallon IV impact timing ('about five decades') from Wikipedia's Metroid Prime plot.

entries.comment: Chozo: Chozo tribes – Thoha and Mawkin
entries.content:
Late in their history the Chozo were divided into tribes, two of which decided the fate of SR388 and ZDR (Metroid Dread). The Thoha were scientists and the peaceful tribe; they colonized SR388, met the X Parasites there and genetically engineered the Metroids as the X's predators. Only the Thoha could control the Metroids. The Mawkin were a warrior tribe led by Raven Beak, whose creed was "Hadar sen olmen", power is everything. The two tribes joined forces to contain the Metroids on SR388 once the creatures had grown beyond control.

When the Thoha resolved to destroy SR388 to wipe out the Metroids for good, Raven Beak, who coveted the Metroids as weapons for galactic conquest, massacred the Thoha. He spared one, the scientist Quiet Robe, because Thoha control over the Metroids was needed for his plans, and took him hostage to the planet ZDR. The last of the Chozo Memories recorded on SR388 preserves this moment: a Chozo warrior standing over the body of another leader, his army arrayed below.

On ZDR Raven Beak intended to wait until the Metroids had wiped out the X on SR388, then return. Instead an X Parasite infected one of his soldiers; every Chozo on ZDR except Raven Beak and Quiet Robe was taken by the X. Raven Beak sealed the infected in the region of Elun and built robotic Chozo Soldiers to replace them. Meanwhile Samus exterminated the SR388 Metroids for the Galactic Federation. Raven Beak then let footage of a living X reach the Federation, reprogrammed the E.M.M.I. units sent to investigate, and lured Samus to ZDR to harvest the Metroid DNA in her body and clone a Metroid army.

Both tribes touched Samus directly. Raven Beak was present when the Chozo adopted her and gave her some of his own DNA. Quiet Robe disabled an E.M.M.I. that was about to kill her in Ferenia, told her the tribes' history, and was murdered by one of Raven Beak's robot soldiers moments after opening her way deeper into ZDR. Samus vowed to avenge him. She defeated Raven Beak aboard his fortress Itorash; an X seized his body, and she destroyed the creature it became. The X that had taken Quiet Robe's corpse later bowed to her and merged with her, neutralizing the Metroid transformation that would otherwise have drained her Gunship, and she escaped as ZDR exploded. With that, the Thoha and Mawkin tribes are extinct. See also Raven Beak, Quiet Robe, Chozo Soldiers, E.M.M.I., Planet ZDR, Chozo Memories.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki has no Thoha/Mawkin pages; built from Raven Beak, Quiet Robe and Wikipedia accounts. Did not claim Samus carries Thoha DNA specifically (unverified); only Raven Beak's contribution is sourced.

entries.content:
Old Bird is a male Chozo of Zebes and the closest thing Samus Aran has to a foster father. Nearly everything known about him comes from the Metroid manga; in the games he is seen only in artwork depicting him beside the child Samus (Metroid: Zero Mission), and he takes no on-screen action in any of them.

Per the manga, Old Bird travelled with Gray Voice to the human mining colony K-2L to request a quantity of afloraltite. There he met the three-year-old Samus, who approached him without fear, and told her: "We look different... but inside... we have the same 'heart' you do..." Her father Rodney Aran was reluctant to part with the ore, but the Chozo left with what they had come for. When the two returned after Ridley's Space Pirates had razed the colony, they found Samus the only survivor and brought her to Zebes to raise.

On Zebes Old Bird oversaw her upbringing. Mother Brain predicted that a frail human body could not survive the planet, so the Chozo integrated their DNA with hers (Gray Voice's, per the manga) and fitted her with a Power Suit. Old Bird taught her that befriending and understanding others can solve problems, a lesson she lived when she befriended the creature Pyonchi, who stayed beside her for years. In her teens he and Gray Voice trained her in the suit. After the Badger Clover incident he told her she was ready to go: "We gave you 'Power'!"; discipline and heart she would have to develop on her own. He added that the Chozo were a declining species and that it was time for her to become independent, and Samus resolved to become the true Protector of the Galaxy.

Old Bird treated Mother Brain as the computer interface overseeing Zebes and routinely asked it for its reports on SR388. When Mother Brain turned and the Space Pirates invaded, he was among the Chozo who escaped while Gray Voice held off Mother Brain and Ridley. His fate after the fall of Zebes is not recorded anywhere official.

For Samus, Old Bird is the gentle half of her Chozo upbringing, the heart to Gray Voice's discipline. She left Zebes with his blessing, carrying the Power he said the Chozo had given her. See also Gray Voice, K-2L, Rodney Aran and Virginia Aran, Mother Brain, Zebes.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki's Old Bird page says Rodney provided the afloraltite; its Samus Aran page says Rodney refused and the Chozo left. Worded to fit both. No in-game on-screen actions found for Old Bird beyond Zero Mission artwork.

entries.content:
Gray Voice (also spelled Grey Voice) is a male Chozo of Zebes who appears only in the Metroid manga. Pragmatic and demanding where Old Bird was gentle, he was the second guardian of Samus Aran's childhood and the Chozo whose genes she carries: when the Chozo gave Samus Chozo DNA so that she could survive Zebes and wear their armor, they used his. As she was told, "In order for you to inherit Chozo genes, we used his DNA." The bond is described as that of a father and daughter of different species, and on at least one occasion Samus could hear his thoughts. (The Mawkin leader Raven Beak later revealed that he too contributed DNA to her; Metroid Dread.)

Gray Voice travelled with Old Bird to K-2L for afloraltite and helped recover the orphaned Samus after the Space Pirate raid, but he opposed the adoption at first: "Old Bird!! What do you plan to do by bringing a human child here." He relented, and in her teens he trained her in the Power Suit without softness; his standard was "You can't be second or third place."

He was also the Chozo who best understood Mother Brain. He praised it as the greatest being in existence and, in the same breath, called it a defective product that had self-programmed its own directive. When Mother Brain seized control of Zebes and the Space Pirates, Gray Voice appeared to side with them. Samus, confronting him, could only ask, "Gray... Voice... Why are you with the Space Pirates..." It was a ruse: he had planned from the start to destroy Mother Brain once its ambitions became clear. He donned a Chozo Power Suit and attacked Mother Brain, inflicting serious damage, until Ridley intervened and struck him a fatal blow. As Ridley moved to finish him he launched a last attack from below that let the fleeing Chozo, Samus among them, escape the Pirate assault. Samus understood only afterward: "Gray planned to destroy Mother from the start... is that right?!"

Ridley, who had killed her parents, thus also killed the Chozo whose blood runs in Samus's veins; and every time she dons the Power Suit she is wearing a legacy that includes his. See also Old Bird, Mother Brain, Ridley, Power Suit.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki's Gray Voice page says Ridley dealt a 'fatal blow' without stating death outright; its Mother Brain page says he was killed by Ridley. Written as killed.

entries.comment: Chozo: Chozo Statues, Item Spheres and Torizo
entries.content:
Chozo Statues are the sentient guardian statues the Chozo left on every world they settled: Zebes, SR388 (where early records call them Artifactor statues), Tallon IV and ZDR. Most are bird-like figures seated or kneeling with hands outstretched, often cradling a sphere. Sculpting them was a sacred practice thousands of years old, entrusted only to Chozo of long experience. In the Chozo's own words, the statues act as sentinels and as storehouses of Chozo secrets and powers; some are reminders and symbols of peace, some exert a subtle influence, and some guard hidden Chozo ways. Those who honor them earn the Chozo's friendship; those who damage them earn the Chozo's anger.

Their practical purpose is to hold the Chozo's gifts. Weapons and suit abilities left for a worthy inheritor rest in Item Spheres in the statues' hands, and Samus has recovered Bombs, beams, suits and much else this way on Zebes, SR388, Tallon IV and ZDR. Some statues restore her instead: resting in their palms in Morph Ball form refills her energy. On Tallon IV the great Chozo Elder statue in the Hall of the Elders launches her along magnetic tracks to hidden chambers, and its eyes ignite when the Turned attack. Space Pirate records note that each of the twelve statues of the Artifact Temple corresponds to one Chozo Artifact.

A few statues are more than sentinels. On Zebes two statues known as Torizo rose to fight Samus (Super Metroid): one in Crateria animated the moment she took the Bombs from its hands and fought on after losing its head; a golden Torizo in lower Norfair, far stronger, caught her Super Missiles and hurled them back, spat explosive item balls from its mouth, swept the floor with shockwaves and guarded the Screw Attack. In Chozodia a Chozo stone guardian, the Ruins Test, holding a mirror image of Samus, tested her when she had only the Paralyzer in hand and then returned her the Legendary Power Suit (Metroid: Zero Mission). Others have exploited the statues' trusted shape: aboard the BSL station an X Parasite mimicked a golden Chozo Statue, its Item Sphere a lure, until Samus destroyed it and regained her Charge Beam; and on SR388 she found a Chozo statue mutilated in its item chamber.

To Samus the statues are the familiar face of her foster people, still handing her their tools long after the sculptors are gone. See also Chozo Lore, Chozodia, Golden Torizo, Chozo Artifacts, X Parasites.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki's Torizo page calls the Norfair one the 'Golden Version'; 'Golden Torizo' used as a cross-reference name only. 'Item Sphere' term taken from Metroid Wiki's Fake Chozo Statue page.

entries.comment: Chozo: Chozo Memories and the Chozo of SR388
entries.content:
The Chozo Memories are a set of images recording the Chozo's history on SR388, recovered by Samus during her Metroid extermination mission on that planet (Metroid: Samus Returns). They are the only first-hand account of how the Metroids came to be.

The record runs as follows. The Chozo came to SR388 and settled it. There they met the X Parasites, native organisms that invade and copy the planet's creatures and that killed everything like a plague. To fight the X, Chozo scientists, the Thoha tribe, engineered the Metroids, energy-draining predators that hunt and consume the X; the name Metroid means ultimate warrior in the Chozo tongue. The Metroids were so effective that they nearly drove the X to extinction, and for a time the Chozo lived in peace. Then the Metroids grew feral and out of control, rising to the top of SR388's food chain and threatening the civilization that had made them. The final memory shows a confrontation between two Chozo leaders: one stands over the other's body, looking out over an army. That figure is Raven Beak of the Mawkin warrior tribe, and the dead are the Thoha, massacred because they meant to destroy SR388 to end the Metroids for good (see Thoha, Mawkin, Raven Beak). The Chozo abandoned SR388 after this, leaving only ruins, their laboratories and the Metroids sealed in the depths.

Everything the galaxy later suffered descends from this record: the Space Pirates' theft of Metroids, the Galactic Federation's extermination order, and the X, which resurfaced once the Metroids were gone and spread to the BSL station (Metroid Fusion). The manga tells it differently, with the Chozo of Zebes discovering the X and hiding them from the Federation, and no Chozo colony on SR388 at all; the record found on the planet itself takes precedence.

Samus has walked every stage of this story. She was raised by Chozo on Zebes, recovered Chozo weapons from the statues in SR388's ruins, destroyed the Metroids the Thoha had made and spared the last hatchling, became host to Metroid DNA, and finally destroyed SR388 itself to end the X. Per the Fusion manual, she is perhaps the most appropriate successor to the Metroids' title of ultimate warrior. The Chozo Memories showed her that the Metroids were never mere monsters but a Chozo weapon that slipped its leash, and that Chozo had killed Chozo over it. See also Metroids, X Parasites, SR388, Chozo laboratories of SR388, Quiet Robe.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki has no Chozo Memories page; the memory-by-memory sequence is summarized from Wikipedia's description, so individual image contents are kept general. Manga/SR388 conflict noted in one clause per instructions.

entries.comment: Chozo: Chozo language and the Chozo Lore of Tallon IV
entries.content:
The Chozo language is a runic script of great complexity inscribed on the walls, gates, totems and statues of Chozo settlements. Samus's Translator Module can render it, though at times with difficulty; Space Pirate linguists fared worse and complained they could not find the Artifacts of Tallon IV until they could decipher the messages carved into the statues of the Artifact Temple. On Tallon IV the Chozo used their writing as locks: paired Runic Symbols on gates must be read and activated to open the way, and the twelve Chozo Totems of the Artifact Temple carry rune clues to the hidden Artifacts. Holobanners, flat orange holograms that vanish when viewed edge-on, bear short messages: The Hall of the Elders; That which fouls the waters seeks the Sun; Only the holder of twelve shall face the Worm; The Great Poison corrupts all, even the Chozo. The spoken tongue is heard on ZDR, where Raven Beak and Quiet Robe speak it; Raven Beak's creed is "Hadar sen olmen", power is everything (Metroid Dread). Samus, raised among Chozo, follows it.

The Chozo Lore is the body of inscribed records the Chozo of Tallon IV left in their own voice, which Samus read during the Phazon incident there (Metroid Prime). It tells of their choice to live simply and in harmony with nature; of visions of past and future they called harmonization with the infinite; of the prophecy of the Worm, a creature born of parasites and nurtured in a poisoned womb that would devour the world, and of a Defender who would face it; of the meteor that brought the Great Poison, Phazon; of the Cradle and the twelve-Artifact Cipher built to contain it; of the Space Pirate infestation; of the Turned; and of the Chozo's own fading and exodus from the physical world.

Its most personal entries concern Samus, whom the Chozo remembered as "the child we found so long ago" and watched across the void. They call her the Hatchling, the Newborn, the Shining One and the Entrusted One: "a fledgling orphaned on a savaged planet", a lone figure "dressed for war" who "hunts the corrupted" and "bears our legacy" in Chozo armor and weapons. They wondered whether she still lived, whether her parents had died to the same creatures, and whether she dreamed of the Chozo, and they left weapons, armor and messages so that she could gather the Artifacts and reverse the evil, something only the Entrusted One could do. Reading these words on a poisoned world, Samus learned that the Chozo's hopes for her reached far beyond Zebes. See also Chozo Artifacts, Artifact Temple, Chozo Ghosts, Tallon IV, Phazon.
entries.notes: The Lore exists in two regional wordings (Hatchling/Newborn vs Entrusted One); both sets of terms are given without meta reference to versions. Overlaps by design with prime1's prophecy entry but centers on language and the records themselves.

entries.content:
Chozo Ghosts, called the Turned in the Chozo Lore, are the spectral remnants of the Chozo of Tallon IV, corrupted by the Great Poison, Phazon. The Chozo's own record describes them as beings utterly corrupted by the Great Poison who still hold to their Chozo forms but whose minds are black with fell intentions: doomed souls in limbo who seek to disrupt the Artifacts that seal the Poison's source. A Holobanner states the cause plainly: The Great Poison corrupts all, even the Chozo. As the Chozo faded from the physical world after the meteor strike, those who did not pass on cleanly became the Turned, driven mad until they could no longer tell friend from foe.

They haunt places of spiritual significance, above all the Chozo Ruins: the Hall of the Elders, where Samus first met them, and the Sunchamber, where the Artifact of Wild lay among spirits drawn to a corrupted, beast-infested site. They phase in and out of the visible spectrum, strike quickly and vanish, and are aggressive and erratic, attacking anything that enters their sacred grounds, yet they can act on the physical world. Natural energies such as fire, ice and electricity pass through them; only the Power Beam and Super Missiles can harm them, and the X-Ray Visor is the one reliable way to track them. Space Pirates studying the Ruins took casualties from them and recorded with satisfaction that even ghosts can be destroyed.

Not every spirit was lost. When Meta Ridley shattered the twelve Chozo Totems of the Artifact Temple, twelve Chozo Ghosts appeared in their place, restored the totems in ethereal form and activated the transport into the Impact Crater, opening the way for Samus to destroy the creature Metroid Prime (Metroid Prime). The Chozo Lore had promised as much: the Chozo's will would persist until the Entrusted One arrived.

For Samus the Turned were a bitter fight. The Chozo who raised her were of Zebes, but the Ghosts wore the shape of her foster people and attacked her in the halls that held the Chozo's last words to her. She destroyed the corrupted and was aided by the sane, fulfilling the Totem's charge to free the spirits. See also Phazon, Chozo Artifacts, Artifact Temple, Meta Ridley, Chozo Lore, Tallon IV.
entries.notes: 'Could no longer distinguish friend from foe' from Wikipedia's character list; combat facts from the Metroid Wiki Chozo Ghost page.

entries.content:
Chozo technology ranks among the most advanced the galaxy has known, and it outlives its makers. Its hallmarks are longevity, modularity and the fusion of machine with living matter.

- Battle armor. The Power Suit is a Chozo invention: modular armor that uploads data, accepts new weapons and modifications and adapts to them at once. Samus's suit was made for her by the Chozo of Zebes (per the manga, Mother Brain modified Chozo battlesuit technology to produce it), and it is partly organic, able to be absorbed into her body and summoned again. The Chozo left a second suit, the Legendary Power Suit, in Chozodia beyond the Ruins Test; only it could use the Plasma Beam, Space Jump and Gravity Suit hidden on Zebes. On ZDR, Raven Beak and his Chozo Soldiers wore armor of the same lineage.
- Weapons and abilities. The Power Beam, Ice Beam, Wave Beam, Plasma Beam, Missile Launcher and Boost Ball are Chozo designs, left for a worthy inheritor in the hands of Chozo Statues. The Chozo of Tallon IV wrote that they left their weapons and armor for the Entrusted One.
- Thinking machines. On Zebes the Chozo built Mother Brain, a supercomputer meant to oversee the planet and bring the galaxy's species into harmony; on Elysia they built the mechanoid Elysians and gave the first of them self-awareness. Both outlived them, and Mother Brain betrayed them.
- Living weapons. The Thoha tribe bioengineered the Metroids on SR388 to hunt the X Parasites.
- Architecture and mechanisms. Chozo structures are so old they cannot be carbon-dated. Tallon IV's ruins hold Holobanners that light themselves, Radiation Collectors that store solar energy, Kinetic Orb Cannons and Spinners that respond to the Morph Ball, color-coded doors that open only to specific weapons, and the Artifact Temple's Cipher of twelve Artifacts. On Elysia, SkyTown's research pods hover on rocket-like engines.

The Chozo also understood what technology costs. Per the manga, the science that gave them long lives compromised their ability to reproduce; on Tallon IV they chose to set advanced technology aside altogether; and they warned younger races such as the Bryyonians to adopt it slowly. Their legacy is double-edged: the Elysians kept faith, Mother Brain and the Metroids turned on the galaxy, and the Power Suit carried Samus. She has spent her career reclaiming Chozo devices from Chozo hands, and she wears their greatest work every day. See also Power Suit, Mother Brain, Elysians, Metroids, Chozo Statues, Legendary Power Suit.
entries.notes: Items listed as Chozo designs are those Metroid Wiki files under Category:Chozo Technology. The Power Suit page's claim that a Chozo scientist 'Dryn' developed the suit could not be verified (no page exists) and was omitted.

result.research_notes:
Research limits: the shared WebSearch budget was exhausted before my first search, so all research used WebFetch only (about 50 fetches). Metroid Wiki has no pages for Thoha, Mawkin, Chozo Memories, Chozo Archives, Chozo Soldier, Chozo Seal, Item Sphere, Itorash, Elun, Ferenia, Metroid Suit, Golden Torizo or Bomb Torizo (all 404). IGN was blocked, StrategyWiki returned 403, and metroid-database.com redirected to an unrelated domain (not followed).

Could not verify / left out: (1) a memory-by-memory description of the eleven Chozo Memories; the entry follows Wikipedia's summary of the arc (arrival, X, Metroid creation, peace, Metroids out of control, final image of one leader over another's body with an army) plus Metroid Wiki's identification of that figure as Raven Beak. (2) The contents of Metroid Dread's Chozo Archives (only unlock captions found). (3) Whether Samus specifically carries Thoha DNA, and whether Raven Beak calls her 'Hatchling' or 'daughter' in Dread; sources only say he was present at her adoption and gave her some of his DNA, so nothing more was claimed. 'Hatchling' and 'Newborn' as Chozo terms for Samus are verified only in the Tallon IV Chozo Lore (one regional wording), with 'Entrusted One' and 'Shining One' in the other. (4) The Thoha's 'low tolerance for violence' (task brief) was not found; sources say 'peaceful'. (5) Old Bird has no on-screen in-game actions per Metroid Wiki; only Zero Mission artwork. (6) 'Dryn' as the Power Suit's developer (Metroid Wiki Power Suit page) has no supporting page; omitted.

Contradictions found: Metroid Wiki's Old Bird page says Rodney Aran provided the afloraltite, its Samus Aran page says he refused; worded to accommodate both. Gray Voice's page says Ridley dealt a 'fatal blow' without stating death; the Mother Brain page says Ridley killed him (written as killed). The manga says there was no Chozo colony on SR388 and the Zebes Chozo hid the X from the Federation, contradicting Samus Returns/Dread; noted in one clause, later sources preferred. Metroid Wiki's Chozo Ruins page says the Chozo came to Tallon IV 'after leaving Zebes' while the SkyTown page says they left Elysia for Tallon IV; the Zebes claim was not used. The Tallon IV Chozo Lore uses different entry names and terms for Samus in its two regional versions; both sets of terms are included without meta reference.

Key-rule notes: bare 'Chozo' only on the overview; 'Golden Torizo' and 'Chozo laboratories' used only as cross-reference names (owned by super-metroid and sr388). 'Chozo DNA'/'Chozo blood' placed on the Gray Voice (donor) entry; expect co-firing with samus-bio's DNA entry, which is intended.
